recipes.name: Easy White Chicken Enchiladas
ingredients_raw: 2 (6 ounce) packages seasoned cooked chicken cubes
1.5 cups white cheese sauce, or queso dip

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Lightly spray an 8x8-inch glass baking dish with cooking spray.

Stir together the softened cream cheese, sour cream, and salsa until blended. Fold in chicken and shredded cheese. Spread a small amount of white cheese sauce onto the bottom of the baking dish. Evenly divide the filling among the tortillas, and roll into firm cylinders. Place into prepared baking dish and cover with remaining sauce.
Bake in preheated oven until golden and bubbly, about 30 minutes. Allow to rest 5 minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy White Chicken Enchiladas
raw_recipe.description: These white chicken enchiladas are a cinch to make with ingredients right off the shelf. The only skill required is in measuring, the rest just works itself out!

review.reviewBody: It's my recipe, of course I love it. Some quick notes: a jar of Tostitos Monterey Jack Queso dip (in the chip aisle) works great for the sauce. Also, depending on the size of your tortillas, sometimes a larger baking dish works better. Enjoy!

This recipe was delicious and adaptable; I do not tolerate dairy very well but love it so am always looking for recipes where you can substitute dairy free ingredients. I followed recipe but substituted the cream cheese with Trader Joe’s dairy free and substituted the sour cream with Elmhurst dairy free. I did use a little cheddar cheese in a roux for the top. ( because I tolerate cheddar most of the time.) which I added a little taco seasoning to. Then baked. It was yummy! Hope this helps those who want less dairy. Thank you for an adaptable recipe!

This is simple and delicious. I made a couple minor tweaks and a mistake and it was still great. My wife isn't a big mexican food fan, but she loved it. I'll definitely make it again. 

The tweaks: I used corn tortillas instead of flour because I like them better. You will likely get about eight enchiladas out of this recipe if you use corn tortillas because they're smaller than flour. I would also microwave a stack of them for 30 seconds under a paper towel to make them easier to roll without breaking. I also added some taco seasoning to the filling on the advice of another reviewer. I recommend both. 

The mistake: I forgot to mix in the shredded cheese with the filling, so I ended up just covering the top with sharp cheddar. It made a nice cheesy crust on top that didn't burn, so I would do that again. Next time I'm going to add some shredded monterey jack to the filling as well. 

Did I mention that this recipe is very easy to make? Try it.

this was AWESOME. I signed up for an account just to rate this. I prefer corn tortillas over flour... it made this recipe feel a little bit heathier when eating it lol. instead of rooling them, I just layered corn tortillas at the bottom and on top, then I put sauce on top and sprinkled the shredded cheese on top (and didnt put it in the middle cuz i forgot to) it was awesome. yummmmmyyy...

I have made these several times. The first time as written and way too bland. After that I add 1/2 package of taco seasoning mix and that totally changes and adds a lot of flavor. I sautee the chicken in olive oil with McCormicks N'Orleans cajun seasoning and cut into pieces. I spray my pan with pan and don't put the sauce in the bottom. I place the sauce on top and the last few minutes sprinkle some shredded cheese on top. My hubby requests at least weekly. With those changes definitely a 5 star recipe!

Very easy recipe, and delicious! I'd suggest to put your corn tortillas in a ziplock or airtight container, and microwave them for 30 seconds before you attempt to roll them. Otherwise you'll end up with torn tortillas and a messy counter :)

It was very good I made some minor changes as well, I bought jalapeño cream cheese and made my own chicken seasoned it with taco seasoning and green chilies and onion. And put diced green chilies in the mixture. The husband and children approve therefore I do!

These were exactly as the recipe stated: easy and delicious. I did use low fat cream cheese, simply for less calorie content, and it still tasted amazing. I ended up with slightly more filling than I had tortillas (I was only cooking for two), so I poured the remaining filling over the top of the enchiladas, and then added shredded cheese over the top of that. SO good, very rich!

My whole family loved this recipe, it is a keeper for sure. The only changes I made was I made my own Monterey Jack Queso, I felt it would be cheesier and creamier than the stuff bought in the store. One of my daughters is gluten free so she was able to eat the chicken mixture so we placed that in a corn tortilla for her and just sprinkled cheese over that and baked, but i am sure if your whole family id gluten free you can find a substitute for flour to thicken the Queso sauce. This is most defiantly a keeper.

My husband loved it. I substituted red salsa and shredded the chicken as I don't like chunks of chicken. I used a can of mushroom soup diluted with 1/2 can of milk instead of the white cheese sauce. The enchiladas were creamy and very tasty. Loved it!!

Ridiculous. The only enchilada I would use the word "decadent" to describe. I used a 9x13" pan though, and stuffed 6 very fat enchiladas in it. As an added toping, I spread some remaining filling on top, followed with a layer of shredded mozzarella cheese and a thin layer of bread crumbs to give it a nice baked crust that added some nice crunchy texture.
The flavor was excellent, but they were just mush after baking. Not sure if there was too much cheese sauce?
read the reviews first so I ditched the cheese sauce and the cream cheese - used more salsa verde and added garlic, onion and a some jalapeno slices - turned out nicely
I've made this several times, it's always a hit with family and friends!
It was amazing! I used the white queso cheese dip and I added extra shredded cheese to the top
This was very good and delicious

Sorry but we’re not a fan of this recipe. We followed the directions exactly. It looked great coming out of the oven and was very easy to make. The filling was good, but needed more spice. However, the Queso cheese sauce over powered the rest of the ingredients making the enchiladas soggy and added an unpleasant after taste. Thanks for sharing the recipe, but we won’t be trying this again.
